No Shizuku app is required. Connect one tablet by USB, authorize USB debugging, then run tools/dwas_EQ_ADB_Enable.bat from the project or release bundle. The BAT starts a restricted dwas_EQ app_process bridge as adb shell (UID 2000) and the app talks to it only through a token-authenticated 127.0.0.1 socket.

The Wired ADB bridge itself ends at reboot. If reboot persistence reacquires Direct Dolby successfully, the BAT is not needed again; rerun it only when Direct Dolby cannot regain control or after reinstalling/updating dwas_EQ for wired diagnostics.

dwas_EQ needs notification permission for its persistent notification and audio features. Open the notification settings below and allow notifications for this app.
ADB access is required to use the app features. Enable USB debugging, connect the cable, then run dwas_EQ_ADB_Enable.bat.
Welcome to the dwas Equalizer app.
Shape your tablet sound with a 9-band equalizer and optional sound effects. Changes are applied only when you choose them, so your original Dolby state stays easier to recover.
Displays the currently detected audio output route, active processing backend, wired ADB connection, and effect status.
Adjust nine frequency ranges from deep bass to high treble. Move a band up to emphasize it or down to soften it. dwas_EQ maps this 9-band curve to the tablet’s existing 20-value Dolby GEQ.
Fine-tune overall headroom, left/right speaker balance, loud peaks, bass and width. Experimental effects are kept in their own tab.
When EQ bands are boosted, loud passages can distort. This lowers the overall level slightly to leave extra room and keep the sound cleaner. Automatic mode follows the largest EQ boost for you.
Lower only the left or right side when one side sounds louder. 0 dB keeps that side unchanged; more negative values make it quieter.

Softens sudden volume peaks before they become harsh or distorted. Attack controls how quickly it reacts, Release how quickly it lets go, Ratio how strongly it limits, Threshold when limiting starts, and Post gain the final level.
Experimental: PresetReverb is attached to the active player session when discoverable, but device/player auxiliary routing can still limit the audible result.
This control becomes available when the connected player and device support the effect.

Adds weight to low-frequency sounds such as kick drums and bass. Start low and raise the strength gradually to avoid booming or distortion.
Makes the stereo image feel wider and more spacious. Strength 0 means no virtualization; higher values increase the effect when the device supports variable strength.

Releases Direct Dolby and Android EQ control sessions held by dwas_EQ, clears Wired ADB authentication, disables Root Dolby opt-in, and removes the external-output override. An active EQ baseline is restored first when available. dwas_EQ cannot revoke the platform capability that allows Direct Dolby or erase approval stored by an external root manager, so Direct Dolby may be detected as controllable again after refresh and root-manager approval must be revoked in that manager if desired. After resetting all permissions, run dwas_EQ_ADB_Enable.bat again to reactivate the application.

EQ and sound effects can raise parts of the audio signal above the original level. Review safe listening guidance and warning symptoms.
dwas_EQ can raise selected frequency ranges above the original signal through equalization and sound effects. High levels and long or repeated listening can stress hearing even when there is no pain.
Lower system volume before using strong EQ, bass boost, virtualization or post gain, then raise levels gradually. Combining multiple boosts can increase peaks and the chance of distortion.

Stop and rest if you notice ringing, fullness, pain, pressure, reduced hearing, difficulty hearing high frequencies, sound sensitivity, dizziness or difficulty understanding speech. Sudden hearing loss may require prompt medical assessment.
The information below explains risks associated with amplified audio in dwas_EQ. Read to the end before deciding whether to agree.

This app can change frequency gain, bass emphasis, stereo widening and limiter post gain. Specific bands can carry more energy and sound louder even when system volume is unchanged. dB values shown by the app are processing gain values, not measured sound-pressure levels at your ear.

Hearing risk depends on sound level together with exposure time and repetition. Long listening at high levels, or repeated high-level exposure, can add to cumulative stress. Use the lowest practical volume and include quiet breaks during extended listening.

Large boosts across several EQ bands and bass controls can increase digital peaks and may cause clipping, tearing, buzzing or harsh sound. If distortion appears, lower system volume and processing gain immediately. The absence of audible distortion does not prove that a listening level is safe.

After loud sound, hearing may temporarily feel muffled or quieter. Repeated excessive exposure can be associated with hearing changes that do not fully recover. Manage volume before discomfort appears because hearing changes can occur without pain.

Ringing, buzzing, hissing or other sounds without an external source may begin or worsen, and everyday sounds may become uncomfortably intense. Stop strong processing if new tinnitus persists or repeatedly returns and consider professional evaluation.

Stop amplified listening and reduce volume if you develop ear pain, pressure, fullness, tinnitus, reduced hearing, a left/right hearing difference, difficulty with high frequencies, poorer speech understanding, dizziness or balance symptoms. Seek medical advice if symptoms are severe or persist.

A sudden marked loss of hearing in one or both ears, especially with strong tinnitus, fullness or dizziness, should not be assumed to be an app setting problem. Stop use and seek prompt medical assessment.
Existing conditions, children and sensitive listeners

If you have hearing loss, tinnitus, sound sensitivity, ear disease, recent ear surgery or ongoing hearing treatment, consider professional advice before strong DSP use. Children and listeners who are sensitive to sound should use more conservative volume and shorter listening periods.

Headphone sensitivity and impedance, built-in speakers, Bluetooth devices, USB DACs, system volume, source mastering, other DSP and fit can all change actual sound pressure at the ear. The same dwas_EQ setting does not mean the same real-world loudness on every device.

Lower system volume before enabling effects, then increase EQ, bass and virtualization gradually from small values. Avoid leaving maximum boost enabled when it is unnecessary, take breaks during long sessions, and do not use excessive levels when you need to remain aware of your surroundings.

dwas_EQ does not measure sound pressure at your ear, your individual hearing condition or a safe personal exposure dose. This notice provides general safety information and is not a medical diagnosis or treatment. Consult an ear or hearing professional if you have concerns.

By agreeing, you acknowledge that the app can alter audio energy and perceived loudness and that safe volume and listening-time management are required. This notice is not intended to waive consumer rights or responsibilities that cannot legally be excluded.
